title: How is a customer roll fee charged on a Container Bookings booking?
content:
## When this applies
This entry covers the Container Bookings product line. A customer roll beyond the tier's free allowance owes one customer roll fee, and the fee is owed from the roll date, whether or not it was charged at that time. A roll whose fee was not charged is charged when the booking is next handled, as long as the booking still accepts amendment charges under the amendment rules.

## Business effect of the charge
Charging the fee adds one customer roll fee entry, dated today, to the booking's charge history and raises the booking's outstanding charges by exactly the amount booked. The booking's sailing, cut-offs, containers and status are not touched.

## How it is invoked
The charge is made with **charge_customer_roll_fee_5e1ab19d**, an internal tool that must first be unlocked (unlock) and then called (call) by the agent. The tool books exactly the amount passed in; it does not compute an amount and does not check any business condition.

## Parameters
| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| booking_id | the booking reference number of the booking being charged, as returned by the booking lookup for the verified customer | identifier |
| vessel_voyage | the vessel and voyage the charged roll moved the booking off, as shown on that roll's entry in the booking's charge history | verbatim: copied character for character, preserving every letter, digit, space and punctuation mark, with no translation, normalisation, addition or deletion |
| fee_usd | the customer roll fee to book, in USD | a positive decimal amount with 2 decimal places; a value given with more digits is rounded half-to-even to 2 decimal places when booked |

## Return
The tool returns a text rendering of a dictionary describing the booked entry: booking_event_id (reference of the new fee entry), booking_id (the booking charged), charge_code (always customer_roll_fee), vessel_voyage (the sailing recorded on the entry), amount_usd (the fee booked, USD with 2 decimal places), event_date (YYYY-MM-DD, the booking date of the entry) and charges_due_usd (the booking's outstanding charges after the fee, USD with 2 decimal places). A returned booking_event_id means the fee is on the account. The entry is recorded with the amendment kind customer_requested_vessel_change, carries the booking's equipment type and records no container count.

## Points of judgement
**Does the call move the booking to another sailing?** No. The roll is already recorded; the call only books its fee.
